2027-02-08.title: First Monday of the Great Fast · Vibhoodi (Ash Monday)
2027-02-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The sin of humanity and its consequence
2027-02-08.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Day of the penitential service (Vibhoodi), with fasting and abstinence from meat.
2027-02-08.verse: leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
theo: The Great Fast has begun. Yesterday was Pethurtha Sunday; the Syriac word means putting an end, turning back, and the calendar explains that the days of rich food and celebration are over. In many Syro-Malabar homes Pethurtha evening is still a family meal shared with some solemnity, a farewell to meat and fish until Easter, and in older Syrian Christian households the vessels used for meat were scrubbed clean or set aside for the whole season. The St Thomas Christians have long called this season the fifty days fast, counted from Pethurtha to Easter. Today, the first Monday, the Church keeps the penitential service called Vibhoodi. The ashes are traditionally made by burning the tender coconut-leaf palms kept from last year's Oshana, and the priest traces a cross with them on our foreheads, recalling the word spoken to Adam: “you are dust, and to dust you shall return.” The calendar asks for fasting and abstinence from meat today, and recommends abstinence throughout the season.

It is striking that the Church opens the Great Fast with the first page of the Bible. “In the beginning when God created the heavens and the earth, the earth was a formless void and darkness covered the face of the deep.” Into that darkness God speaks: “Let there be light”; and there was light. Again and again the refrain returns: “God saw that it was good.” The fast is not contempt for the body or for the good things of the world; it is God's word speaking again over the void and darkness in us, bringing order and light. Joshua stands where we stand today, at the edge of a river. Moses is dead, the Jordan lies ahead, and God says: “Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.” He gives Joshua one method for the crossing: “This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth; you shall meditate on it day and night.” Paul names what went wrong with humanity: people “exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator.” Fasting puts the creature back in its place, so that the Creator may be first again. And Paul is not ashamed: the gospel “is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith.”

In the Gospel Jesus says he has come “not to abolish but to fulfill” the law, and he carries it into the heart. Not only murder, but anger and insult are judged. Then he describes a scene every Christian knows: “So when you are offering your gift at the altar, if you remember that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.” This is why the Vibhoodi is a penitential service of reconciliation. Ash on the forehead and peace in the home belong together. A fast that gives up fish and meat but keeps a quarrel alive has missed the heart of the matter. Seven weeks lie ahead: dust that knows it is dust, light that God speaks into the dark, courage for the crossing, and a brother or sister waiting for our first step.
outline: Ask: what does the ash on your forehead say to you this morning?
Vibhoodi and the fifty days fast.
The fast as God's new creation in us.
Joshua at the Jordan; the word day and night.

live: Decide today, with your family, what you will give up for the whole Great Fast, and what the saving will be given to.
Call, visit or write to one person who has something against you, before Sunday.
Read one chapter of a Gospel every day of the Great Fast.
2027-02-08.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, at the beginning of this holy fast you mark us with ashes and remind us that we are dust. Speak your light into our darkness, give us courage for the crossing of these days, and do not let us bring our gift to your altar while a brother or sister waits for our pardon. Make this Great Fast a time of new creation for us and for our families. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Before the Holy Qurbana we make peace with one another; Jesus asks that our gift at the altar come from a reconciled heart.

quick: The Great Fast begins: we are dust, and God is our life.
God says again, “Let there be light”; the fast is a new creation.
First be reconciled, then offer your gift.
2027-02-08.action: Take the first step of reconciliation with one person today.
2027-02-08.question: Who has something against me, and what is my first step?

family.explain: Jesus says: if you come to church with a gift for God and remember that your brother is upset with you, leave the gift, go and make peace first, and then come back. God wants our hearts at peace with one another before we pray together.
family.intention: We pray for families where people are not speaking to one another.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family to whom we need to say sorry today?”

illus: Two brothers near Pala had not spoken for six years because of a boundary wall between their plots. On the morning of the Vibhoodi the younger one stood in the line for the ashes and found himself just behind his elder brother. When the priest said the words about dust, he thought: our wall will outlast both of us. After the service he walked over and said only, come home for tea. The wall is still there, but the gate in it is open now.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we begin the Great Fast before you. Make us dust that is open to your breath. Amen.
share: Let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Where do I need God's light this Lent?
Be strong and courageous (Joshua 1:9). What crossing lies before me in these seven weeks?
First be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). With whom must I make peace?
pm.resp: Lord, create a new heart in us.
interc: For the whole Church as she begins the Great Fast.
For all who are estranged from their families.
For the poor, who will receive what our fast saves.
For those who find fasting difficult because of illness or age.
For our group, that we may keep this fast with joy.
pm.close: Father, you call us back to you with fasting and prayer. Reconcile us with you and with one another, and lead us through these days to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, this morning the ash has marked our foreheads. The words remind us of the first sin and its sentence: you are dust, and to dust you shall return (Genesis 3:19). Yesterday was Pethurtha; the feasting is over, and the fifty days fast has begun.

But the Church gives us today the first page of the Bible. God speaks into the darkness: let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Again and again he looks at what he has made and sees that it is good. The fast does not despise God's gifts. It makes room for God to create us anew.

Like Joshua at the Jordan, we stand at the edge of a crossing. God says to us too: be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go (Joshua 1:9). And he gives us his word to carry, to meditate on day and night.

Jesus goes to the heart of the matter: if you remember at the altar that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there and go; first be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). Let the ash on our foreheads lead to peace in our homes. Then our fast will be pleasing to God. Amen.
kids: Children, today the priest put ash on our foreheads in the shape of a cross. It means: I belong to Jesus, and I want to start again. Is there someone you need to say sorry to today?

intro: Theme: “first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.”
The ash of the Vibhoodi, the first light of creation, Joshua's courage, and the peace Jesus asks before the altar.

q: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; you are dust, and to dust you shall return.
For he says, “At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.” See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Write down today what you will fast from, and keep the note in your Bible.

sub: God saw that it was good.

So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
points.apply: Ask God each morning of this week to speak his light into one dark corner of your life.

sub: The gift left at the altar.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!

concl: The Great Fast begins with ash and with light: we are dust, and God speaks over us again.
Be strong and courageous, and let the first fruit of the fast be peace.
